section_summary.extract_value: This section discusses the key findings of a study examining the relative effects of goal frame, goal content, and goal proximity on trainees' self-regulatory activities and learning/performance outcomes. The results indicated that goal content was more potent than goal frame or goal proximity. The study also explored goal frame-goal content congruence, finding that learning-focused conditions were generally more beneficial than performance-focused conditions, and examined the effects of goal proximity and self-regulatory processes on learning and performance.
